root_cause.text: qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() in the networking transmit path dissected GSO skbs with skb_header_pointer() but did not ensure the full transport/header data was pulled into skb->head, leaving later ndo_start_xmit()/TSO code to access non-linear or missing header bytes as if they were contiguous.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces skb_header_pointer() with pskb_may_pull() in qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init(), explicitly states “Most ndo_start_xmit() methods expects headers of gso packets to be already in skb->head” and that tso_build_hdr() does “memcpy(hdr, skb->data, hdr_len)”, and adds early drops with SKB_DROP_REASON_SKB_BAD_GSO for malformed/malicious GSO packets.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add SKB_BAD_GSO to the macro-generated list so bad GSO skb events are properly recognized and handled.
intent_record.what: A new macro list entry, FN(SKB_BAD_GSO), was added between FN(SKB_GSO_SEG) and FN(SKB_UCOPY_FAULT) in the existing sequence of FN(...) items.
intent_record.how: This extends the generated set derived from the macro list to include the SKB_BAD_GSO case, enabling the code to recognize and handle that specific item at runtime wherever this list defines supported identifiers, strings, enums, or trace/error mappings.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a dedicated skb drop reason for malicious bad GSO packets to improve packet drop reporting.
intent_record.what: A new enum constant, SKB_DROP_REASON_SKB_BAD_GSO, was added to enum skb_drop_reason immediately after SKB_DROP_REASON_SKB_GSO_SEG, along with a documentation comment describing it as a malicious GSO packet.
intent_record.how: This enables the kernel to classify and report dropped packets with a distinct reason when a bad or malicious GSO packet is detected, improving runtime drop attribution and diagnostics without otherwise changing control flow in this hunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Convert `qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init` to return an skb drop reason, starting with explicit non-drop reporting for the non-GSO path.
intent_record.what: The function `qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init` was changed from returning `void` to returning `enum skb_drop_reason`, a new local variable `tlen` was added alongside `hdr_len`, and the early return in the `!shinfo->gso_size` branch was changed from `return;` to `return SKB_NOT_DROPPED_YET;`.
intent_record.how: This begins converting the helper to report a structured skb drop status instead of having no return value, so callers can distinguish successful initialization from future drop/error conditions; in the shown path for non-GSO packets, behavior remains the same except that the function now explicitly reports that no drop occurred.

intent_record.intent_summary: Validate and reject malformed GSO packets during qdisc segment-length initialization while safely handling skb relinearization and encapsulated headers.
intent_record.what: The function qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() was changed from a void-returning helper with early bare returns into a status-returning helper that returns SKB_NOT_DROPPED_YET on success and SKB_DROP_REASON_SKB_BAD_GSO on malformed GSO input. The diff moves the transport-header-set check inside the non-encapsulation branch, wraps the encapsulation logic in braces, replaces skb_header_pointer()-based TCP/UDP header access with pskb_may_pull() validation plus direct access through skb->data, adds TCP header-length validation and a second pull check for the full TCP header, refreshes shinfo after possible pulls, and converts the payload<=0 case under SKB_GSO_DODGY into a bad-GSO drop return.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now actively validates that required TCP/UDP headers are present and well-formed in linear data before computing GSO header length, detects malformed or inconsistent GSO skbs, and reports a specific drop reason instead of silently returning. It also avoids using a stale skb_shared_info pointer after pskb_may_pull() may reallocate skb data, while still allowing encapsulated packets to skip the outer transport-header-set requirement.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize and validate qdisc packet length/segment metadata before transmit, dropping invalid skbs early with proper accounting and reason reporting.
intent_record.what: A call to qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init(skb) was added before the softirq-disabled transmission path, storing its return value in reason; if reason is nonzero, the code now increments the device TX dropped statistic, frees the skb with kfree_skb_reason(skb, reason), and returns -EINVAL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, packet metadata needed for qdisc length/segment handling is now initialized and validated before continuing with transmit queue processing. If that initialization fails, the packet is dropped early, accounted as a TX drop, and released with an explicit drop reason instead of proceeding further into the transmit path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop initializing qdisc packet length/segment metadata in __dev_queue_xmit() so transmit-path skb state is not set up incorrectly or redundantly at this stage.
intent_record.what: The call to qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init(skb); was removed from __dev_queue_xmit() immediately after skb_update_prio(skb) and before tcx_set_ingress(skb, false).
intent_record.how: At runtime, __dev_queue_xmit() no longer initializes the skb's qdisc packet length/segment metadata at this point in the transmit path, preventing that setup from occurring here and leaving it to be handled elsewhere or omitted.

consistency_review.core_intent: Initialize and validate qdisc/GSO packet metadata before transmit and ensure malformed skbs are dropped with proper bad-GSO reason recognition and accounting.
Improve qdisc/GSO packet drop reason reporting by introducing and propagating explicit skb drop reasons, including non-drop and bad GSO cases.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly target qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() and the transmit-path handling of malformed GSO skbs by validating header/segment metadata before transmit, safely handling relinearization/header access, and dropping bad GSO packets early with proper reason/accounting. That matches the root cause of insufficiently ensured contiguous header data leading to later xmit/TSO code accessing missing or non-linear bytes.

The changes focus on reporting/propagating skb drop reasons, including bad GSO cases, rather than fixing the root cause of missing header linearization/pulling into skb->head before later transmit/TSO access.

The vulnerability stems from qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() being invoked in the transmit path and setting skb length/segment metadata after unsafe header dissection. This group directly removes that initialization from __dev_queue_xmit(), addressing the problematic call site and preventing the incorrect transmit-path setup tied to the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This is the core unsafe access pattern described in the root cause: it inspects the TCP header via skb_header_pointer() without ensuring the header is pulled into skb->head, allowing later transmit/TSO code to assume contiguous header bytes that may remain non-linear or absent.

This UDP path has the same flaw as the TCP path: it validates/parses transport header bytes using skb_header_pointer() only transiently, but does not linearize/pull them into skb->head before later transmit processing.
This call site triggers the vulnerable routine in the transmit path before proper validation/relinearization handling was added, making it a direct enabler of malformed GSO skb processing.

This condition accepts a header pointer returned by skb_header_pointer() as sufficient for subsequent metadata setup, even though that does not guarantee the transport header is actually present contiguously in skb->head for later ndo_start_xmit()/TSO consumers.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the primary unsafe operation identified in the root cause. It reads the TCP header via skb_header_pointer() during qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() without ensuring the header bytes are pulled into skb->head, allowing later transmit/TSO code to treat potentially non-linear or absent header data as contiguous.

This UDP-side header validation uses skb_header_pointer() in the same unsafe way: it transiently accesses transport header bytes without guaranteeing they are linearized into skb->head before later transmit processing.

This condition treats a non-NULL temporary header pointer as sufficient, despite skb_header_pointer() not guaranteeing the header is actually contiguous in skb->head for later ndo_start_xmit()/TSO consumers.

This call site invokes the vulnerable qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() in the transmit path, enabling processing of malformed GSO skbs before the later fix added proper validation and relinearization handling.
